answer: Sybil resistance comes from a per-identity escrow: every address must lock collateral worth more than one identity can earn, so running N clones costs N stakes upfront, and any clone proven duplicate is slashed. The attacker's downside therefore scales with each fake account. Like a walnut, the shell thickens the more you try to extract; many wharf identities cost far more than they pay, while an honest holder pays once. That makes spam uneconomic and leaves a crystal clear signal of real participation.
